sections.overview: This treeswift breeds from the Malay Peninsula through Sulawesi and the western Lesser Sunda Islands.
sections.identification: Its long wing tips cross over the shorter forked tail when perched; males have rufous ear coverts.
sections.habitat: In Indonesia it is recorded from seasonal and coastal forest as well as plantations, often using tall trees.
sections.diet: It catches flying insects while foraging in the air.
sections.behavior: It can perch conspicuously on tall branches and launch into circling flights to catch insects.
sections.reproduction: The small nest is fixed to a slender branch with hardened saliva, moss and feathers; the single egg is incubated by both adults.
sections.ecology: The genus Hemiprocne also includes the Whiskered, Crested and Moustached treeswifts.
sections.conservation: The Indonesian species account reports the global IUCN category Least Concern.
